Apply a batch of REGRESSION fixes to /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts and /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-detect.ts (Nxeon migration engine). These are confirmed regressions introduced by a recent hardening sweep, found by an adversarial review. Edit only these two files. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` (stay green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. Read each cited region before editing; line numbers are approximate (the file shifted). Report per-fix final line numbers. Preserve all existing honest gates; never make a migration less safe.

## 1. [CRITICAL — DATA LOSS] External DB volume created empty + F3 skips external volumes → silent blank DB
The external-VOLUME pre-pass (search `externalVols`, `docker volume create`, near the external-network pre-pass) auto-creates any `external: true` volume that's missing. But the F3 empty-volume guard (search `volExternal`, `restoreVolumes`, `hardEmptyVol`, the stateful regex, `-mindepth 1 -print -quit`) EXPLICITLY SKIPS external volumes (`if (!srcKey || volExternal.has(srcKey)) continue;`). So a DB datadir on an `external: true` volume that didn't migrate gets created empty → the DB inits blank → reported "running". 
FIX: make F3 ALSO empty-check external volumes — remove the `volExternal.has(srcKey)` skip from the F3 stateful empty-check loop, KEEPING the `restoreVolumes` exemption (a volume F1 will restore into is legitimately empty). So an empty external DB volume is hard-refused (named) unless a restore is pending. Verify both the compose-path and standalone-path F3 guards. Do NOT change the pre-pass creation itself (external NETWORKS still auto-create fine); just ensure an empty external DB volume can't silently start.

## 2. [HIGH] rsync `-A -X` makes exit 23/24 a failed copy though data landed
`rsyncPull` now uses `rsync -aHz -A -X --numeric-ids` (search `-A -X`). rsync returns exit **23** (partial transfer due to error — typically an ACL/xattr the destination fs or SELinux rejects) or **24** (vanished source files) while THE FILE DATA STILL TRANSFERS. Every callsite treats non-zero as failure (search `r.code === 0`, `r.code !== 0` in the copy loops: app dirs, docker volumes, cron, letsencrypt, unit files, ssh-keys), and the tar-fallback regex (search `code 1[27]|unexpectedly closed`) doesn't include 23/24, so it declares the dir uncopied though the bytes are on disk.
FIX: treat rsync exit 23 and 24 as SUCCESS-with-warning at the rsync exit-code checks. Cleanest: introduce a small helper `rsyncOk(code) => code === 0 || code === 23 || code === 24` (or inline the check) and use it at the app-dir copy success check AND every other `rsyncPull` result check where `=== 0`/`!== 0` gates success (volumes, cron, letsencrypt, reference config, unit-file pulls, ssh-keys). When code is 23/24, still count it copied but push a brief note ("some file attributes/ACLs weren't preserved on the new server"). Be careful to only apply the tolerance to rsync results, not to non-rsync `sh` calls that legitimately use exit codes.

## 3. [MEDIUM] Host Mongo/Redis detection false-fails on a leftover stopped install
The host mongo/redis dump block (search `host-mongo`, `host-redis`, `command -v mongod`, `command -v redis-server`, `/var/lib/mongodb`, `/var/lib/redis`) runs unconditionally and treats a non-dumpable result as `failed` "data NOT migrated". A source with a stopped `redis-server`/`mongod` (leftover dependency) or an empty `/var/lib/redis` → scary false failure.
FIX: only treat it as a migratable DB (and thus emit a `failed`/named step on dump trouble) when the service is actually RUNNING — add `pgrep -x mongod`/`pgrep -x redis-server` (or `systemctl is-active`) to the detection, AND/OR only fail when the datadir is non-empty. A stopped/leftover install with no data should be silently skipped, not reported as lost data. Keep the real dump path for a live service unchanged.

## 4. [MEDIUM] Image pre-flight refuses a `build:` stack instead of letting compose build it
The compose image pre-flight (search `config --images`, `ensureImage`, `imageBlock`) sets `imageBlock` and skips the whole project when an image can't be transferred — even for a service that has a `build:` context (which `compose up` would build locally from the copied build dir).
FIX: parse `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}${projArg}config --format json` once; build a set of images that belong to a service WITH a `build:` section. When `ensureImage` fails for such an image, do NOT set `imageBlock` — emit a warning ("<image> will be built on the new server from its build context") and let `up -d` build it. Only hard-block (imageBlock) for a NON-build image that can't be transferred/pulled.

## 5. [MEDIUM] PHP auto-detect over-fires on a stray `.php`
The WEB-1 PHP doc-root detection (search the `find ${s.root} -maxdepth 2 ... -name '*.php'`) marks any doc-root with any `.php` as a PHP app → installs php-fpm + rewires the vhost to FastCGI, which can execute files a static site served as text.
FIX: require a STRONG signal — `index.php` at the doc-root root, OR `wp-config.php`, OR `artisan`, OR `composer.json`. Drop the bare `-name '*.php'` anywhere-in-tree signal (or keep it only as a weak tiebreaker that still requires one of the strong markers).

## 6. [LOW] container_name clash guard over-claims from override files
The guard greps `container_name:` across ALL `ce.composeFiles` (search `grep -hE '^\\s*container_name:'`, `claimedNames`), so an override redefining a name claims both the base and override names → can falsely skip an unrelated project. 
FIX: derive the effective container_names from `config --format json` (`.services[].container_name`) — the authoritative merged names — instead of the raw multi-file grep. (You'll already be parsing `config --format json` for fix #4; reuse it.)

## 7. [LOW] External-network/volume owner-prefix strips hyphens
In the pre-pass (search the `match(/[a-z0-9]+/g) || []).join("")` computing `project`), stripping hyphens makes `my-app` → `myapp`, so the `willCreate`/`ownedVols` exclusion never matches compose's real `my-app_<key>` names.
FIX: compute the prefix the way compose does — lowercase and keep `-`/`_` (strip only truly-invalid chars), or key the exclusion off the F2 `projArg`/source project name used at bring-up.

## 8. [LOW] nftables target-refuse: wrong-server wording (+ optional accept-check)
The OS-3b nftables branch (search `nftablesDropPolicy`, the openWebPorts nftables case) runs on the TARGET but the message says "the OLD server used an nftables ruleset". 
FIX: reword to "this (new) server". Optionally suppress the advisory when the ruleset already accepts 80/443 (nice-to-have; the wording fix is the required part).

## 9. [LOW] Wire up (or remove) the dead honest-refuse detections
`migrate-detect.ts` computes `altProxies`, `nonSystemdInit`, `nftablesDropPolicy` but a repo-wide grep finds NO consumer in worker/. The intended honest "we found Caddy/HAProxy / non-systemd init — these weren't auto-migrated" steps never render. VERIFY this (grep the fields in worker/migrate-real.ts). If genuinely unconsumed, WIRE THEM UP: in the migration run, read these from the scan/plan and `push` one honest `copied`-status step per finding (alt proxy names / non-systemd init dirs), matching the honest-refuse style. Thread them from detect→plan if needed (they're on ScanResult; check they reach `items`/`scan` in the worker). If wiring is too invasive, at minimum leave a clear TODO — but prefer wiring since the silent-drop is the whole thing these were meant to fix.

## 10. [LOW/edge] Apache LimitRequestBody 2 GB cap
`LimitRequestBody ${bodyLimit(s) * 1024 * 1024}` can exceed the 2 GB signed max on Apache. Cap the emitted byte value at `2147483647`.

## Also: fix the two stale COMMENTS that say redis is in the hard-refuse stateful set (the regex correctly omits redis — the code is right, the comments are wrong).

## Constraints
- Fixes #1 and #2 are the priority — get them exactly right. Reuse existing helpers; validate interpolated values; single-quoted `sh -c '…'`.
- Do NOT regress the working parts the review verified sound (A12 copy-with-notice, F1 dump/restore, F2 projArg, A1 clobber, config_files replay, EnvironmentFile, timers, accounts, Apache WS, gRPC gating).
- Finish only when tsc is clean and both test files pass. Report per-fix final line numbers and, for #9, whether the detections were already consumed or you wired them.
